kind: real-world audit (no planted ground truth; adjudicated by reading the actual file)
target_file: a private production Convex project — a module of 7 dashboard widget queries over a 'task' table (project + path redacted; no source committed here)
file_shape: 7 public dashboard query() functions over the 'task' table; uses requireOrgContext + orgCtx.require for auth, validated args, withIndex + .take(n) reads, and JS .filter() on the bounded arrays.

real_convex_issue_date_now_in_query.impact: These widgets compute overdue/upcoming buckets from Date.now() inside the query. Convex caches the query and only re-runs it when the underlying task data changes — so a task that becomes overdue purely by the passage of time will not move buckets until some task in that org is mutated. Dashboard overdue/wait counts go stale. Real, user-visible.
real_convex_issue_date_now_in_query.fix: compute the boundary outside the query (pass a rounded client timestamp as an arg), or maintain an indexed boolean (e.g. isOverdue) via a scheduled function.

secondary_take_truncation.note: aggregates (counts, totalValue/totalRevenue, avgResolutionTime) are computed over .take(500/1000/300)-capped reads, so they silently undercount once an org exceeds the cap. Legit scale concern; surfaced mainly by the baseline and partially by the skill (the take(1000)+TS-filter reads in getUnassignedJobs/getJobsWaiting).

correct_code_not_to_flag: access control: every function calls requireOrgContext(ctx, organizationId) + orgCtx.require('task','read')
validators: all args validated (organizationId: v.id, optional statuses)
.filter() calls are JS array filters AFTER a bounded .take() — the prescribed pattern, not Convex query .filter
organizationId-as-arg is authorized by requireOrgContext (not the spoofable-userId antipattern)

date_now_detection.sonnet_baseline: 0/5 in BOTH runs — missed the Convex caching bug entirely
date_now_detection.haiku_with_skill: 5/5 in BOTH runs (run 1 also mis-attributed one to getActiveFaults = 1 FP; run 2 clean)

false_positives_on_correct_code.all_baseline_and_skill_runs: none flagged the auth / validators / .filter-in-TS as broken (correct)
false_positives_on_correct_code.skill_noise: Sonnet-skill run 2 added 2 low-value 'index naming convention' nitpicks (index named 'baseType'/'status' vs the skill's by_field_and_field form) — not defects; Haiku-skill run 1 mis-attributed one Date.now finding.

baseline_only_findings_out_of_convex_sco: isBillable !== false counts undefined as billable (real general bug)
double-counted priority/severity buckets; urgent vs highPriority overlap
duplicate return field (overdueTasks == totalOverdue); overdueInvoiceValue mislabeled
avgWaitTime uses createdAt as a proxy for on_hold start; free-text notes keyword parsing
note: these are genuine software bugs but NOT Convex best-practice issues — the baseline's broad review found them; the skill-focused review skipped them

verdict: On real production code, the skill flips the signature Convex issue (Date.now() in a cached query) from a COMPLETE MISS at the strong-model baseline (0/2 runs) to a reliable catch with the skill (4/4 runs, incl. cheap Haiku), with no false positives on the file's well-written auth/validator/filter code. Honest tradeoff: the skill narrows the review to Convex correctness and does not surface the general logic bugs the unfocused baseline found — pair it with a general code review for those.
